title: The Wreck of the Coral Triangle
premise: Ines Dravenmoor, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted from two countries, salvages a river-locked chest bearing the seal of Vhaloria, a nation erased from maps forty years ago. The chest contains a ledger of debts owed to the drowned state — including one in Ines's late mother's name — and both the Vhalorian remnant underground and the cartel that sank the nation will kill to control it. Pursued upriver toward the forbidden source valley where Vhaloria's last archive lies submerged, Ines must decide whether the debt is a burden or an inheritance. At the source, Ines floods the archive rather than surrender it, pays the debt with the truth instead of the treasure, and walks away free but no longer certain which memories were ever truly theirs.
about_author: Edmund Vane is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade charting tributaries in contested borderlands before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people the maps forgot, from a houseboat he refuses to anchor in any one country for longer than a season.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Ines Dravenmoor, guiding a smuggling run to pay down a crushing debt, watches the river cough up a bronze chest stamped with Vhaloria's drowned seal. POV: Ines. Beat: restless survival curdling into fatal curiosity — the moment a debt becomes a destiny.

chapters.title: A Ledger of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Opening the chest in a riverport safehouse, Ines finds a debt ledger listing names of the erased nation — the last entry in their mother's handwriting. POV: Ines. Beat: grief and suspicion, as inheritance and trap become indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Men Who Buy Silence
chapters.summary: Cartel broker Sef Ondar arrives offering to buy the chest whole; Ines refuses, and the safehouse burns behind them. POV: Ines. Beat: the price of refusal made immediate — flight, smoke, and the first blood on Ines's hands in years.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Ines barges passage upriver with ferrymaster Odile Vasse, who recognizes the seal and demands a share of whatever the source holds. POV: Odile. Beat: wary alliance; two people who trust no one agreeing to trust each other exactly once.

chapters.title: What the Blacklist Forgets
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the Alpine disaster that got Ines blacklisted — a client abandoned, a truth buried. POV: Ines. Beat: shame examined; the reader learns the debt Ines carries is moral before it is financial.

chapters.title: The Remnant at Kiln Reach
chapters.summary: A river town of Vhalorian exiles claims the chest as national property; their archivist, Tam Reyle, offers safe passage in exchange for it. POV: Ines. Beat: temptation of belonging — a home offered at exactly the wrong price.

chapters.title: Ondar's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Cartel gunboats strike Kiln Reach at dawn; Tam is taken, the ledger page naming Ines's mother is stolen, and Odile runs the blockade. POV: Odile. Beat: guilt compounding — Ines's refusal now has a body count.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Odile teaches Ines the river's hidden channels while the two trade confessions in the dark of the wheelhouse. POV: Odile. Beat: love against duty begins its quiet argument — Odile's duty is her boat; Ines's is the dead.

chapters.title: The Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: They raise a submerged Vhalorian bell that hums when the source draws near, a navigational relic — and a homing beacon Ondar can also hear. POV: Ines. Beat: wonder shadowed by dread; the past is literally calling them in.

chapters.title: Tam's Testimony
chapters.summary: Rescued Tam reveals the cartel didn't just sink Vhaloria's treasury — they forged the debt ledger to launder the theft. POV: Tam. Beat: betrayal reframed; Ines's mother's entry may be forged, and Ines must choose what to believe.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Names
chapters.summary: A canyon wall carved with every Vhalorian name lost in the sinking; Ines finds their mother's name among them, freshly chiseled. POV: Ines. Beat: devastating midpoint revelation — the mother was there, at the end, on purpose.

chapters.title: Odile's Anchor
chapters.summary: Ondar's men board at night; Odile scuttles her own ferry to stop them, losing her livelihood and her past in one act. POV: Odile. Beat: sacrifice — duty and love finally pointing the same direction, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Three Days on Foot
chapters.summary: The trio climbs toward the source valley on rations for two, and hunger forces a vote on whether to turn back. POV: Ines. Beat: the price of survival made literal — democracy at the edge of starvation, and Ines votes to go on.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: They reach the valley: a flooded archive city beneath a glacial lake, Vhaloria's entire memory preserved in cold water. POV: Ines. Beat: awe — the destination exceeds every rumor, which makes the coming choice unbearable.

chapters.title: Ondar Arrives First
chapters.summary: The cartel has a second team already diving the archive; Ondar offers Ines their mother's true file in exchange for safe passage out. POV: Ondar. Beat: the devil's reasonable offer — truth as currency, priced in complicity.

chapters.title: The File
chapters.summary: Ines reads the mother's file alone: she was the archivist who chose to sink Vhaloria rather than let Ondar's employers have it. POV: Ines. Beat: the inheritance revealed — not a debt but a decision, waiting to be repeated.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Cold
chapters.summary: Ondar's divers breach the archive vault; Tam is shot defending the master ledger, and the lake begins to drain through the breach. POV: Tam. Beat: climax ignites — loyalty, greed, and water all converging at once.

chapters.title: What Ines Breaks
chapters.summary: To stop Ondar, Ines collapses the archive's seal gates, drowning Vhaloria's memory forever — the same choice their mother made. POV: Ines. Beat: the climax's terrible symmetry; survival purchased with erasure.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Ondar, refusing to leave empty-handed, follows Ines onto the collapsing spillway; Ines offers rescue and Ondar chooses the ledger instead. POV: Ines. Beat: the antagonist's epitaph — a man who drowned reaching for paper.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Ines burns the surviving forged ledger pages at the source, freeing every name on them, including their mother's. POV: Ines. Beat: release — the debt was never owed to the dead, only to the truth.

chapters.title: Two Tickets, One River
chapters.summary: Odile's salvaged skiff carries them downstream past the burned safehouse and Kiln Reach; Tam survives, and the exiles begin writing a new ledger of the living. POV: Odile. Beat: tenderness after ruin — love chosen freely, duty redefined as the people you keep.

chapters.title: The Guide Who Walked Away
chapters.summary: At the river's mouth, Ines mails the blacklist countries a confession of the Alpine disaster, then signs on as Odile's deckhand with no debts and no map. POV: Ines. Beat: resolution — survival finally paid for in full, and worth the price.
